resources.string: Adds \"Pinyin\" to the text-selection menu. Highlight Chinese anywhere, tap it, and read the selection with pinyin above each character.
Keep a persistent notification with an on/off button.
Red 1, orange 2, green 3, blue 4, grey neutral.

There are two ways to read pinyin.

Highlight text
Select any Chinese text, then tap Pinyin in the selection toolbar. On ColorOS it usually sits behind the ⋮ overflow button, next to Translate and Copy. The selection opens with pinyin above each character.

Whole screen
Annotates every text block on screen with cards drawn over it. This one needs the Android accessibility permission — the app walks you through it. Text inside pictures, games and video subtitles cannot be read, so it stays unannotated.

Either mode can be switched on and off from the notification or the Quick Settings tile.
The update cleared the accessibility permission. Tap to switch Pinyin Lens back on.

The update cleared the accessibility permission, so whole screen has stopped working.

Android does not let an app restore this itself — it must be granted from system settings. Open settings takes you straight to the Pinyin Lens toggle.

If the toggle is greyed out
ColorOS re-applies its restricted-settings block after each sideloaded update. Go to Settings → Apps → Pinyin Lens → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then switch it on.

Whole screen needs the Android accessibility permission, because reading the text on screen is the only way to know what to annotate. Pinyin Lens only reads text — it does not record or send anything.

1. Tap Open settings below.
2. Under Downloaded apps (or Installed services), choose Pinyin Lens.
3. Switch it on and accept the prompt.
4. Come back here — whole screen switches itself on.

If Android says the setting is restricted
That happens with sideloaded apps. Go to Settings → Apps → Pinyin Lens → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then try again.

On ColorOS
Also allow auto-start and remove battery restrictions for Pinyin Lens, or the system may switch the service off later.
Annotates every text block on screen with cards drawn over it. Needs the accessibility service. Text drawn as graphics — games, video subtitles, pictures — cannot be read and stays unannotated.
Reads the text on screen so it can be redrawn with pinyin above each character.
Character size in the sheet you get after tapping Pinyin.
Scales the cards relative to the text they cover, so a caption stays smaller than body text. Turn it down to make cards spill less onto what is underneath.
